The second argument of `then(a, b)` only handles a rejection from before the `then()`. If `a` itself throws, `b` is not called. A `catch()` after the `then()` handles both.

The rule only reports a `then()` call with two arguments that is a statement of its own. One that is returned, awaited, assigned, or followed by more of the chain is not reported.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
loadItems().then(render, showError); // an error in render is not handled
```

{/* bad */}
```js
loadItems().then(null, showError);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
loadItems().then(render).catch(showError);
loadItems().catch(showError);
```

{/* good */}
```js
function refresh() {
  return loadItems().then(render, showError);
}
```
